title: Processing of identified data during account registration
description: Homeowner provides personally identifiable information (name, email, etc.) during account registration, which is processed by the Home Hub system.

title: Linking through unique identifier during enrollment
description: Homeowner's account registration involves unique identifiers (email, username, device ID) that can be used to link data across systems.

title: Identifiers in data flow metadata
description: Data flow metadata may contain identifiers about the homeowner and device being enrolled, potentially exposing identity information during transmission.

title: Excessive data type sensitivity in camera/sensor enrollment
description: Camera and sensor data collection may capture more sensitive personal data than functionally required for basic device enrollment.

title: Fine-grained data granularity during device enrollment
description: Enrollment process may collect device configuration data at a more granular level than necessary for basic functionality.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and enrichment
description: Camera/sensor data may be further analyzed, enriched, or processed beyond what is needed for the enrollment functionality.

title: Data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: Enrolled device data may be accessible to more parties (e.g., service providers, third parties) than functionally required for the enrollment process.

title: Unawareness of data processing during enrollment
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of the extent of data collection, processing, and storage that occurs during camera/sensor enrollment.

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: Homeowner may have limited ability to set preferences or consent regarding how personal data is processed during and after enrollment.

title: Difficulty in rectification or erasure of enrolled data
description: Homeowner may lack control to easily correct incorrect data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant after device enrollment.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: GDPR-related concern: System may process more personal data than actually needed for the enrollment functionality.

title: Temporary Access Code as Identifier
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest serves as a unique reference that could identify the specific access event and potentially link to the guest's identity within the home security system.
assumptions: The access code is logged or stored in a way that could be traced back to the guest
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether the access code is actually stored or logged by the system

title: Access Code Observable in Transit
description: The access code transmitted from the guest to the Home Hub could be observed by eavesdroppers, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the home.
assumptions: The access code is transmitted without encryption or is transmitted in a way that can be intercepted
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the transmission security measures in place

title: System Response Reveals Access Status
description: The Home Hub's response (door unlock or denial) reveals whether the access code was valid, which could be used to infer information about the guest or the security system's state.
assumptions: The system provides observable feedback (door movement, sound, light) that reveals the outcome
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether the system provides observable feedback

title: Access Code Retention Beyond Functional Need
description: The Home Hub may retain the access code longer than necessary for the immediate door unlocking function, creating unnecessary privacy risk.
assumptions: The system stores access codes for audit, logging, or future reference purposes
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the actual retention policy of the Home Hub

title: Limited Guest Control Over Access Code
description: The guest has limited control over how the access code is generated, used, and potentially shared, with no clear mechanism to revoke or modify it.
assumptions: The guest cannot easily change or cancel the access code once entered
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the guest's actual control mechanisms

title: Potential Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: The Home Hub may process more personal data than strictly necessary for the door unlocking function, such as logging access codes beyond what's needed for immediate access control.
assumptions: The system logs access codes for purposes beyond immediate functionality
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the actual data processing practices of the Home Hub

title: Quasi-identifier combining sensor events
description: Motion, door, and sensor events can be combined to create a quasi-identifier profile of household activity patterns, potentially linking to specific individuals or households.
assumptions: Events contain timestamps and event types that can be correlated

title: Revealing attributes in sensor events
description: The type, timing, and frequency of sensor events (motion, door openings) can reveal information about household occupancy, routines, and presence patterns.
assumptions: Event metadata includes timestamps and event types

title: Data type sensitivity - sensor data collection
description: Motion and sensor events may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic home automation purposes.
assumptions: Home Hub collects detailed sensor data

title: Excessive volume of event data
description: Continuous logging of all motion/door/sensor events may exceed what is functionally needed for the system's purpose.
assumptions: All events are logged without filtering

title: Unawareness of processing - data subject
description: Data subjects (household members) may not be aware that their sensor events are being logged and stored.
assumptions: No explicit notification or consent mechanism

title: Lack of control - preferences
description: Users may lack control over what sensor data is collected, how long it is stored, or how it is used.
assumptions: No user preferences or consent controls

title: Duration/retention - excessive storage
description: Event data may be retained longer than functionally needed in the local event log.
assumptions: No retention policy or automatic deletion

title: GDPR - Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing more personal data than actually needed may violate GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR applies to the system

title: Processing of identified data at source
description: Home Hub processes and uploads video clips that contain identified information about individuals captured by the camera, including faces, activities, and locations.

title: Data type sensitivity at source
description: Video clips are highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for the home security system's intended purpose.

title: Identified information in metadata during transit
description: Video files in transit may contain metadata (timestamps, device identifiers, location data) that can be used to identify data subjects and link the data to specific individuals.

title: Data propagation during transit
description: Video data is transmitted to cloud storage where it may be accessible by additional services or parties beyond the intended recipient.

title: Processing of identified data at destination
description: Cloud Video Storage processes and stores video clips containing identified information about individuals, enabling identification and potential profiling.

title: Excessive party exposure at destination
description: Cloud storage may make video data accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including cloud service providers, administrators, or third parties with access to the storage system.

title: Excessive data retention at destination
description: Cloud storage may retain video clips longer than functionally needed for home security purposes, violating storage limitation principles.

title: Lack of data subject control at destination
description: Data subjects have limited control over how their video data is stored, accessed, or shared once uploaded to cloud storage, with minimal ability to set preferences or consent.

title: GDPR data minimization violation at destination
description: Processing and storing video data may violate GDPR data minimization principle if the data is more extensive than necessary for the stated security purpose.

title: Linking through unique identifier in motion alert
description: Motion alerts forwarded from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend may contain unique identifiers (e.g., user ID, device ID, or location data) that can be used to link the alert to a specific individual, potentially enabling tracking or profiling across systems.
assumptions: The motion alert data includes identifiers or quasi-identifiers that can be used for linking purposes.

title: Processing of identified data at source
description: The Home Hub (P1) processes and forwards motion alert data that may contain identified information about the data subject, such as user identifiers or device-specific information that can be used to identify the individual.
assumptions: The motion alert data includes user-identifying information that is processed by the Home Hub before forwarding.

title: Excessive data type sensitivity in motion alerts
description: The motion alert data forwarded from the Home Hub may contain more sensitive personal data than functionally required for the intended purpose of alerting the mobile app backend, potentially including location data or other sensitive attributes.
assumptions: The motion alert includes data types that are more sensitive than necessary for the basic alert functionality.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing by data subject
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and forwarded from the Home Hub to the Mobile App Backend, as this may occur without explicit user consent or notification.
assumptions: Users are not informed about the collection and forwarding of their motion data to the backend system.

title: Detection through observed communications in transit
description: Motion alerts transmitted from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend may be observable by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially revealing information about the user's presence or activities.
assumptions: The data flow is not adequately protected, allowing interception or observation of the motion alert data in transit.

title: Identified information in notification metadata
description: The motion-detected notification may contain metadata (e.g., user ID, device ID, timestamp) that directly identifies the homeowner receiving the notification.

title: Linking through unique identifier in notification
description: The notification may include unique identifiers (user ID, device ID) that can be used to link this motion data to other data about the homeowner across systems.

title: Detecting through observed communications
description: The notification itself reveals that motion was detected at a specific time, allowing an observer to infer when the homeowner is present at the property.

title: Excessive data type sensitivity
description: Motion detection data may be more sensitive than functionally required for a simple notification, as it reveals presence patterns and occupancy information.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Homeowners may not be aware that their motion detection data is being processed and transmitted to their device beyond the notification itself.

title: Lack of control over notification preferences
description: Homeowners may lack control over how motion notifications are configured, including frequency, sensitivity thresholds, and which motion events trigger notifications.

title: GDPR data minimization violation
description: Processing motion data for notification purposes may violate data minimization principles if the data collected exceeds what is strictly necessary for the notification functionality.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in aggregated analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., device type, location patterns, usage frequency) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individual users when combined with external data sources.
assumptions: Aggregated data may still retain enough detail to enable quasi-identifier linking when cross-referenced with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Assuming aggregation is not sufficiently anonymized to prevent quasi-identifier linking.

title: Profiling through device usage analytics
description: Device-usage analytics data can be analyzed to identify patterns and behaviors that link back to specific individuals, enabling profiling of user habits, preferences, and activities.
assumptions: Analytics vendor has capability to analyze patterns in the shared data to profile individuals.
uncertainty_note: Depends on analytics vendor's processing capabilities and intent.

title: Quasi-identifiers in aggregated data
description: The aggregated device-usage analytics may contain combinations of attributes that are unique to or highly characteristic of specific data subjects, enabling identification despite aggregation claims.
assumptions: Aggregation may not be sufficient to prevent identification through quasi-identifier analysis.
uncertainty_note: Assumes aggregation methodology may not fully protect against quasi-identifier identification.

title: Data propagation to external vendor
description: Personal data is propagated to an external analytics vendor (EE3) where it may be accessible beyond the original functional scope of the mobile app backend.
assumptions: The external vendor may use the data beyond the intended analytics purpose.
uncertainty_note: Assumes vendor may have broader access than functionally necessary.

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined set of external parties (cloud analytics vendor) beyond what may be functionally necessary for the mobile app's core functionality.
assumptions: The analytics vendor is a known, static party in the data sharing arrangement.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the vendor relationship is predetermined and static.

title: User unawareness of data sharing with external vendor
description: Data subjects (users) may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with an external cloud analytics vendor (EE3).
assumptions: Users are not informed about this specific data sharing arrangement.
uncertainty_note: Depends on privacy policy transparency and user consent mechanisms.

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their device-usage analytics data is shared with external analytics vendors.
assumptions: No granular consent mechanism exists for this data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Assumes consent mechanisms may be broad or non-existent for this specific data type.

title: External vendor receives personal data beyond functional necessity
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) receives personal data that may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, depending on the vendor's internal data sharing practices.
assumptions: External vendor may share or further process the data with additional parties.
uncertainty_note: Depends on vendor's data governance and sharing policies.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The processing of device-usage analytics by the external vendor may involve more personal data than is actually needed for the stated analytics functionality.
assumptions: Analytics vendor may process data beyond what is functionally required.
uncertainty_note: Depends on vendor's actual data processing practices and compliance.

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The DataStore contains video clips that are identified with specific homeowners/users. When retrieving video for playback, the system processes identified personal data tied to individual data subjects.

title: Video data contains unique user identifiers
description: Stored video clips are associated with specific homeowner accounts through unique identifiers, enabling identification of the data subject from the video data.

title: Linking through video metadata identifiers
description: Video data in transit may contain metadata (timestamps, device IDs, user IDs) that can be used to link the video content to specific individuals or their activities.

title: Video data type sensitivity
description: Video content is inherently sensitive personal data that captures visual information about individuals, their activities, and potentially their environment, which may be more sensitive than functionally required for simple playback.

title: Video data propagation risk
description: Video data retrieved for playback may be accessible to or propagated to other services beyond the immediate playback functionality, increasing exposure risk.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: The Mobile App Backend may process video data at a finer granularity than needed for playback, potentially extracting or analyzing more detail than functionally required.

title: Homeowner unawareness of video retrieval
description: The homeowner (data subject) may not be aware when their stored video clips are being accessed or retrieved by the backend system for playback.

title: Limited homeowner control over video processing
description: Homeowners may lack control over how their video data is processed, stored, or shared by the Mobile App Backend beyond basic playback functionality.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing video data for playback may involve collecting and processing more personal data than strictly necessary for the functional goal of video playback.
